sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report documents unauthorized transactional activity identified on account C12265-K2 belonging to customer C12265. Between 2016-12-03 and 2016-12-03, the financial institution detected an abnormal transaction burst comprising 1 unauthorized transaction(s) (including ID(s) 3509359). Total fraudulent exposure identified across the flagged activity amounts to $125.08 USD. All suspicious transactions were conducted through the electronic online payment channel, bypassing physical card-present point-of-sale security controls. Digital identity telemetry reveals that the unauthorized orders originated from a digital device signature (Trident/7.0 | Windows 10 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080) that had never previously interacted with the cardholder's legitimate account. Further technical inspection confirmed that network traffic routed through an evasive proxy configuration designed to obfuscate the perpetrator's physical geography. A graph traversal analysis linked the identical device fingerprint to suspicious transactions on at least 25 other cardholder accounts, including C11010-K1, C10971-K1, C11293-K1, C12897-K1. When contacted by fraud operations, the legitimate cardholder formally repudiated the charges and confirmed the card remained in their continuous physical possession. The observed activity represents a coordinated multi-account compromise using shared device infrastructure, consistent with sophisticated cyber-enabled payment fraud under Rule R9. In accordance with institutional fraud policy and FinCEN guidelines, the compromised card was immediately blocked from further authorization, and connected accounts were placed under heightened continuous surveillance.
